user_query: Identify the protein's likely function, cellular processes, subcellular localization, membrane topology, domain architecture, and strongest homolog-based annotations. Pay particular attention to the N-terminal and internal hydrophobic segments, possible signal peptide or transmembrane helices, catalytic motifs, and whether the sequence resembles a receptor, transporter, enzyme, or signaling/scaffold protein. Clearly separate curated evidence from sequence-based inference.

warnings: Sequence-derived estimates assume an unmodified protein and do not account for processing, PTMs, bound ligands, or oligomers.

function: The M ring may be actively involved in energy transduction.
subcellular_location: Cell inner membrane; Multi-pass membrane protein; Bacterial flagellum basal body
subunit: The basal body constitutes a major portion of the flagellar organelle and consists of four rings (L,P,S, and M) mounted on a central rod. The M ring is integral to the inner membrane of the cell and may be connected to the flagellar rod via the S ring. The S (supramembrane ring) lies just distal to the M ring. The L and P rings lie in the outer membrane and the periplasmic space, respectively.
